newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eko Stahl Q1 sales, orders grew double digits.
newsitem.headline: Eko Stahl Q1 sales, orders grew double digits.

text.p: Loss-making east German steel maker Eko Stahl said on Tuesday its first quarter sales grew 10 percent from the year-earlier quarter, while incoming orders grew 15 percent.
The company aims to cut its 1997 loss to below 100 million marks, after losing 123 million marks last year, marketing manager Eckhardt Hoppe told journalists at the Hanover Industry Trade Fair.

This year is a make-or-break year for Eko, the last year it will receive its 100 million mark subsidy from the BvS German privatisation agency for former state-owned east German firms, said chairman Hans-Joachim Krueger.
This year, Eko must at least complete a sound foundation for future profits, Krueger said.

"We have to get on our own two feet," Krueger said. Belgium's Cockerill Sambre holds a 60 percent stake in Eko, and has an option to buy the remaining 40 percent from the BvS by the end of the decade, which Krueger said he believes it will exercise.
The increase in first-quarter sales was mainly due to the improved business climate for steel. Sales for the full year should be roughly equal to last year's 1.4 billion marks, Hoppe said.
Steel makers were finally able to raise customer prices over the past few months, after a bad year in 1996, he said.
Eko aims to produce 2.0 million tonnes of crude steel this year, up slightly from 1.95 million tonnes in 1996.
-- Terence Gallagher, Hanover Trade Fair newsroom
